articles.title: Nadella's Microsoft Is About to Cut 5,700 Jobs. Xbox May Never Recover.
articles.excerpt: A 2.5% workforce reduction across sales, consulting, and gaming is expected as early as next week — with the Xbox division bracing for what insiders call the largest single layoff event in gaming history.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella at a company event
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft is one of the largest H-1B employers in the US. Thousands of Indian engineers in Redmond, Hyderabad, and Bangalore face an uncertain July as the company restructures around AI — and the 60-day visa clock starts ticking for anyone caught in the cuts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Visa, Mastercard, and Google Just Launched a Stablecoin. It Has 140 Partners and Zero Fees.
articles.excerpt: Open USD, backed by a consortium that includes BlackRock, Stripe, and Coinbase, is designed to become the default digital dollar for global payments — and it could reshape how NRIs send money home.
articles.image_caption: A Bitcoin coin alongside financial data and credit cards on a desk
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans send over $100 billion in remittances annually. A zero-fee, consortium-backed stablecoin endorsed by the payment networks they already use could dramatically lower the cost of moving money between the US and India — if RBI regulations allow it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tata Communications Has Replaced Its CEO, CFO, and CTO in Five Months. A Data Centre Fire Explains Why.
articles.excerpt: The Indian telecom giant's third C-suite appointment of 2026 brings in an Akamai and AT&T veteran as CTO, as the company races to rebuild credibility after a devastating fire at its New Delhi data centre and accelerate its AI infrastructure push.
articles.image_caption: Server racks in a modern data centre highlighting network infrastructure
articles.nri_angle: Tata Communications runs the backbone infrastructure that connects India's digital economy to the world — and its data centres are where many NRI-facing services actually live. A leadership reset of this scale at a Tata Group company signals both crisis and ambition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pichai's Google Ran Out of GPUs. So It's Paying a Rocket Company $920 Million a Month.
articles.excerpt: Google capped Meta's Gemini access, leased compute from SpaceX, and still can't keep up with demand. The AI infrastructure crisis is no longer hypothetical.
articles.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google, at a 2023 event
articles.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai's compute crunch directly affects Indian engineers at Google Cloud and Meta, and downstream capacity for Indian IT firms building on Gemini Enterprise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Just Opened a Factory That Makes Data for Humanoid Robots. Production Workers Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: Apptronik's Robot Park in Austin is training fleets of Apollo 2 humanoids with Google DeepMind's AI. Real deployments start in 2027.
articles.image_caption: A humanoid robot in a digital network setting, representing the new wave of AI-powered automation
articles.nri_angle: Indian AI researchers at Google DeepMind are driving the Gemini Robotics models, while Indian logistics workers in the US face the automation wave these robots will bring.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FactSet's Indian-Origin CEO Just Plugged Google's AI Directly Into Wall Street's Terminal.
articles.excerpt: Sanoke Viswanathan, a former JPMorgan executive, is partnering with Google Cloud to build agentic AI for the financial industry. The tools 40,000 Indian-origin finance professionals use daily are about to change.
articles.image_caption: Financial market data and analytics displayed on a trading screen
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin CEO Sanoke Viswanathan leads FactSet's AI transformation, directly affecting tens of thousands of Indian finance professionals on Wall Street who use FactSet daily.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Narayen Is Leaving Adobe. Both Candidates to Replace Him Are Also Indian.
articles.excerpt: After 18 years, Adobe's Hyderabad-born CEO is stepping down — and the two frontrunners to succeed him, David Wadhwani and Anil Chakravarthy, are also of Indian origin. The diaspora's grip on American enterprise software is tightening.
articles.image_caption: Shantanu Narayen, Adobe's outgoing CEO, who has led the company for 18 years
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin executives dominate Adobe's C-suite — outgoing CEO Narayen and both leading successors are of Indian descent, extending the diaspora's leadership pipeline in enterprise software alongside Nadella at Microsoft and Pichai at Google.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Is Spending $1 Billion to Embed AI Engineers Inside Your Company. The Talent Pool Is Heavily Indian.
articles.excerpt: AWS's new forward-deployed engineering unit will send pods of AI specialists directly to enterprise clients. With Amazon cutting 30,000 corporate jobs while hiring thousands for this initiative, the shift has implications for Indian tech workers on both sides.
articles.image_caption: The Amazon Spheres at the company's Seattle headquarters — the tech giant is deploying  billion to embed AI engineers inside enterprise clients worldwide (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Amazon's massive Indian workforce — both in the US on H-1B visas and in India — makes the diaspora the largest talent pool for this new high-demand role. The initiative also signals which AI jobs are safe from automation and which are not.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Marvell's Stock Just Jumped 7%. Its Largest Lab Outside California Is in India.
articles.excerpt: As the chip company races to build the optical backbone of AI data centres, its biggest R&D hub in India is designing the connectivity silicon that Nvidia, Amazon, and Microsoft need to keep their GPU clusters running.
articles.image_caption: Marvell Technology, the semiconductor firm whose stock surged 7% on its custom AI chip strategy (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Marvell's largest global R&D hub outside its California HQ is in India, making Indian engineers central to the design of connectivity chips that power the world's AI data centres — a story of diaspora engineering influence at the hardware layer.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's UPI Just Went Live in Athens. The Payment System That Replaced Cash Now Works in 10 Countries.
articles.excerpt: Greece becomes the latest country to accept India's real-time payment rails, in a Eurobank partnership witnessed by Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal — and NRI travellers are the immediate beneficiaries.
articles.image_caption: A contactless QR code payment being made via smartphone (Pexels)
articles.nri_angle: NRI travellers to Greece, Singapore, France, UAE, and six other countries can now pay with the same UPI apps they use at home — no currency conversion fees, no card surcharges, no cash anxiety.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bajaj Got Ransomware. Tata Got Hacked. Then a Data Centre Burned Down. India Inc Had a Terrible June.
articles.excerpt: Three cybersecurity incidents at major Indian conglomerates in three weeks have exposed the gap between India's manufacturing ambitions and its ability to protect the systems that underpin them.
articles.image_caption: A cybersecurity professional monitoring systems on a computer screen in low light
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors hold billions in Tata and Bajaj stock. NRIs working at Apple, Tesla, and Qualcomm — all Tata Electronics clients — now have to wonder whether their employer's supplier can protect their work product.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Infosys Just Touched ₹1,000. TCS Lost ₹2,050. The Worst IT Selloff Since Covid Has a Familiar Villain.
articles.excerpt: Every major Indian IT stock fell 2-3.5% on Tuesday as AI deflation, weak guidance, and a global spending freeze converge. NRI investors who held through the pandemic may be staring at round-trip returns.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: Indian IT stocks are among the most widely held equities by NRI investors. TCS and Infosys are also among the largest employers of H-1B workers in the US — when their stock craters, hiring freezes follow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Krishna's IBM Just Built a Chip Smaller Than One Nanometre. It Packs 100 Billion Transistors.
articles.excerpt: The 'nanostack' architecture stacks transistors in 3D for the first time, pointing to a decade of continued scaling — and raising questions about where India fits in the atomic-scale chip race.
articles.image_caption: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna at SXSW 2025
articles.nri_angle: IBM's Indian-origin CEO Arvind Krishna leads the company behind the world's most consequential chip breakthrough, while India's own semiconductor ambitions remain focused on packaging and assembly rather than foundational transistor research.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Built Its First Chip in Nine Months. It Used AI to Design It.
articles.excerpt: The Jalapeño inference processor, developed with Broadcom, could cut ChatGPT's serving costs by half — and signals that AI companies are done renting Nvidia's hardware.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, whose company designed its first in-house AI chip in nine months (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers are deeply embedded across Broadcom, TSMC, and OpenAI's own India operation under new MD Prabhjeet Singh; cheaper AI inference accelerates the disruption pressure on Indian IT services companies.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'If Coding Becomes Automated, Why Are We Needed?' Nilekani Has an Answer.
articles.excerpt: The Infosys chairman used his annual general meeting speech to confront AI's existential threat to Indian IT — arguing that the bigger the disruption, the bigger the opportunity for services firms.
articles.image_caption: Infosys co-founder and chairman Nandan Nilekani
articles.nri_angle: Over 300,000 Indian IT professionals in the US on H-1B visas face direct career implications as AI reshapes the services industry that employs them; Infosys's 28% stock decline this year has hit NRI investor portfolios hard.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Signed a 35-Nation Pact to Secure AI's Silicon Supply Chain. Here's What It Actually Means.
articles.excerpt: At the second Pax Silica Summit in Washington, India committed to building trusted chip and critical-mineral pipelines alongside the US, EU, and 32 other countries — a move that could reshape careers and investments for the diaspora.
articles.image_caption: A semiconductor wafer — the silicon foundation of the AI supply chain India is now helping to secure
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American chip engineers at Intel, Qualcomm, and NVIDIA stand to benefit from deeper US-India semiconductor cooperation, while India's 85,000-job chip workforce target creates new return-to-India career paths and investment opportunities for NRIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Arora's Palo Alto Networks Just Hit a $3 Billion Quarter. Then Its Stock Hit an All-Time High.
articles.excerpt: The Indian-origin CEO bought $10 million of his own stock when it crashed on AI fears. It has since more than doubled. Palo Alto's record Q3 shows why cybersecurity is the AI boom's biggest beneficiary.
articles.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, Chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, at a technology conference
articles.nri_angle: Arora, an IIT Varanasi alumnus, leads the most valuable cybersecurity company in the world — a sector where Indian engineers are in surging demand. NRI investors tracking Indian-origin CEO-led stocks now have a cybersecurity entry point alongside Nadella's Microsoft and Pichai's Alphabet.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Just Bet $48 Billion on India. Jassy Flew to Delhi to Tell Modi Personally.
articles.excerpt: The largest tech investment commitment to India — ever — includes $21 billion for AI and cloud infrastructure alone. Amazon, Microsoft, and Google have collectively earmarked $80 billion for Indian compute capacity in eight months.
articles.image_caption: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy, who met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi to announce the $48 billion investment
articles.nri_angle: AWS's $21 billion cloud expansion creates thousands of new cloud/AI roles for Indian-American engineers, while Amazon stock offers NRI investors direct exposure to India's booming digital economy without the complexity of Indian equities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Just Hired an IIT-IIM Grad to Run India. He Built Uber's Indian Empire First.
articles.excerpt: Prabhjeet Singh, who turned Uber from a ride-hailing app into an auto-rickshaw platform, will lead OpenAI's push into its second-largest market.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman; the company has appointed former Uber India president Prabhjeet Singh as its first India Managing Director (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: IIT-IIM alumni pipeline now reaches frontier AI leadership; OpenAI's India expansion means new AI jobs in Mumbai/Bengaluru for returning NRIs and signals pricing/product changes that affect diaspora developers using ChatGPT APIs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Taiwan Just Raided Super Micro's Offices Over $2.5 Billion in Missing Nvidia Chips. India Should Be Watching.
articles.excerpt: The chip smuggling probe expands as prosecutors search six homes and three companies. For India's semiconductor ambitions, the lesson is about trust as much as technology.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia AI chips — Taiwanese authorities have raided Supermicro offices over .5 billion in missing Nvidia processors allegedly diverted to restricted markets (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers at chip companies face heightened export compliance scrutiny; India's semiconductor ambitions (Tata, Micron Gujarat) depend on being seen as a trusted manufacturing hub in the US-led chip export control regime.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian IT Is Already Making $12 Billion from AI. The Hard Part Is What Comes Next.
articles.excerpt: Nasscom says a quarter of Indian tech firms have moved AI from pilot to production. But JP Morgan's analysts see revenue compression, not expansion. Both sides have a point.
articles.image_caption: Indian IT firms including TCS, Infosys, and Wipro now generate over 2 billion annually from AI-related services (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Indian IT stocks (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) need to parse the gap between Nasscom's bullish AI revenue data and JP Morgan's bearish guidance cuts; engineers considering return-to-India moves should note the shift toward AI-specialist hiring.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Tata Breach Just Got Worse. iPhone 18 Pro Supplier Maps and Drop-Test Photos Are Now on the Dark Web.
articles.excerpt: A Reuters review of newly leaked files reveals component-to-supplier maps, confidential Apple watermarks, and factory photographs of unreleased iPhones — escalating what was already India's biggest corporate cyber breach.
articles.image_caption: Tata Electronics, which assembles iPhones at its Hosur plant, has suffered a breach exposing supplier schematics for Apple's iPhone 18 Pro (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's 26% share of global iPhone production rests on Tata's credibility as Apple's newest major assembler. NRI engineers at Apple, TSMC, and Qualcomm face professional fallout as supplier relationships are exposed; investors in Tata Group companies confront a trust deficit with no clear resolution timeline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: JP Morgan Just Told Indian IT to Brace for Year Two of AI Deflation. The Numbers Are Getting Worse.
articles.excerpt: A new research note warns that every major Indian IT company faces Q1 FY27 guidance cuts as AI-led pricing erosion enters its second year — and this time, deal closures are stalling too.
articles.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bengaluru — JP Morgan warns that Indian IT firms face a second year of AI-driven revenue deflation (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Hundreds of thousands of Indian nationals on H-1B visas work at or are subcontracted through these firms; hiring freezes and reduced onsite deployment directly affect visa renewals and green card pipelines. NRI investors hold significant positions in IT stocks that have collectively shed $26 billion in market value this quarter.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mehrotra's Micron Just Posted a $41.5 Billion Quarter. The Man from Kanpur Has Never Had a Hand This Good.
articles.excerpt: Revenue up 346%, margins at 68%, and $22 billion in locked-in customer commitments. The Indian-American CEO who co-founded SanDisk is running the only American company that makes the memory chips AI cannot function without.
articles.image_caption: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, the Kanpur-born co-founder of SanDisk
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American CEO Sanjay Mehrotra, born in Kanpur and educated at BITS Pilani, runs the only US maker of the memory chips powering the AI boom. His company is also building a $2.75B plant in Gujarat — creating jobs and entry points for India's semiconductor ambitions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A War 5,000 Miles Away Is Slowing India's Chip Dreams. Tata's Dholera Fab Is Hit Hardest.
articles.excerpt: The West Asia conflict has disrupted supplies of helium, bromine, and sulphur — exotic materials that India's greenfield semiconductor fabs need and cannot yet source independently.
articles.image_caption: A researcher handles a silicon wafer inside a semiconductor fabrication facility
articles.nri_angle: NRI semiconductor engineers eyeing return-to-India roles at Tata or Micron face a new variable: project timelines pushed back 6-12 months as supply chains India doesn't control buckle under geopolitical stress.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: South Korea Just Bet $576 Billion on Chips. India Has Bet $10 Billion. That Ratio Tells a Story.
articles.excerpt: Samsung and SK Hynix will build four new mega-fabs as the AI memory race intensifies. India's chip projects face delays and a 50-to-1 investment gap.
articles.image_caption: A silicon wafer at a semiconductor fabrication plant — South Korea has committed 76 billion to dominate the global chip race while India has invested a fraction of that.
articles.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian Americans work at semiconductor firms like Intel, Qualcomm and Micron — Korea's massive bet reshapes the global chip talent map and raises questions about India's ability to compete.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Big Tech Is Buying Into India's Startups — Without Buying Them
articles.excerpt: Meta, Google, Microsoft and Amazon are choosing minority investments over acquisitions in India's $394 billion startup ecosystem. Last week alone, Indian startups raised $1.1 billion.
articles.image_caption: SgtShyGuy via wikimedia (CC0)
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors who backed India's startup boom await returns as the market matures — Big Tech's strategic investment model offers new exit pathways but demands defensible technology over user acquisition.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Just Broke a Decade-Long Rule Because AI Made Hackers Too Fast
articles.excerpt: The company is pushing iOS security patches ahead of schedule for the first time, citing AI-driven threats. For India's booming cybersecurity sector and its 500 million smartphone users, the shift hits close to home.
articles.image_caption: Apple Park in Cupertino, California — the company has broken its own patching schedule to push emergency security updates against AI-accelerated exploits.
articles.nri_angle: India is Apple's fastest-growing major market and already enforces some of the world's strictest patch timelines through CERT-In. Indian-origin cybersecurity leaders like Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora are driving the defensive AI push, while Indian IT services firms are repositioning as cybersecurity providers for global enterprises.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nadella, Pichai, and Arora Just Bought a Cricket Team at Lord's. They Paid £145 Million.
articles.excerpt: A consortium of eleven Silicon Valley executives, most of Indian origin, outbid Sanjiv Goenka to take a 49 per cent stake in London Spirit — the most expensive franchise deal in The Hundred's history.
articles.image_caption: Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks, who led the Silicon Valley consortium's bid for London Spirit
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin tech CEOs who run America's biggest companies are now buying up global cricket franchises, with Indian or Indian-origin investors holding stakes in five of eight Hundred teams — a cultural and financial statement for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The AI Boom Just Made Your MacBook 42% More Expensive. India Got the Worst of It.
articles.excerpt: Apple raised MacBook and iPad prices by up to ₹70,000 in India — the steepest hikes of any market — as AI data centres vacuum up the world's memory chip supply.
articles.image_caption: A MacBook Air keyboard — Apple's laptops in India now cost up to 42 per cent more due to AI-driven memory shortages
articles.nri_angle: Indian tech workers who buy their own laptops face steep cost increases, while NRIs lose the pricing arbitrage that made India trips a chance to buy Apple devices at a discount — a direct consequence of the AI infrastructure boom.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Qualcomm Is Spending $14 Billion to Break NVIDIA's Grip on AI. Its Indian-Origin CFO Is the Architect.
articles.excerpt: A $4 billion software deal and a potential $10 billion chip acquisition signal the most aggressive AI pivot in semiconductor history — with thousands of Indian engineers at the centre.
articles.image_caption: Qualcomm headquarters in San Diego, California
articles.nri_angle: Qualcomm employs thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B visas and its Indian-origin CFO Akash Palkhiwala is architecting the company's $14B AI acquisition strategy — directly relevant to NRI semiconductor professionals and investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nadella's Microsoft Is Being Sued for Overhyping AI. Indian Investors Have the Most to Lose.
articles.excerpt: A securities fraud class action alleges Microsoft misled investors about Copilot adoption and Azure AI performance. The stock has already dropped 10%.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella at a company event
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft under Indian-origin CEO Satya Nadella faces a securities fraud lawsuit over AI product claims — directly affecting NRI investors and Indian employees holding RSUs, who are among the most concentrated MSFT holders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Just Told 4 Million Motorcycle Owners to Go Electric. The Deadline Is 2028.
articles.excerpt: India's capital commits $1.59 billion to its most aggressive EV policy yet — with cash incentives, a petrol two-wheeler ban, and a Chinese platform deal that complicates everything.
articles.image_caption: Electric two-wheelers in India — Delhi has ordered 4 million petrol motorcycle owners to go electric by 2028
articles.nri_angle: Delhi's $1.59B EV policy directly impacts NRI investors holding Tata Motors, Mahindra, and Ola Electric stock, and reshapes the purchase calculus for anyone considering returning to India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Apple Calls India's Antitrust Case a Copy-Paste Job. A Potential $38 Billion Fine Says Otherwise.
articles.excerpt: In its sharpest legal volley yet, Apple told India's Competition Commission that its investigators didn't investigate — they just parroted PhonePe and Paytm. The watchdog has heard this before, from Google, and it didn't care.
articles.image_caption: Apple Park headquarters in Cupertino, California
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American app developers who build for the App Store face real consequences from CCI's outcome — and NRI investors hold significant Apple stock in a company now making 26% of the world's iPhones in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta Handed WhatsApp to an Indian Founder. It Paid $900 Million for the Privilege.
articles.excerpt: CRED's Kunal Shah becomes the first India-built entrepreneur to run a three-billion-user platform. Meta's bet is that his fintech instincts can unlock WhatsApp's commerce ambitions.
articles.image_caption: Kunal Shah, founder of CRED and newly appointed global head of WhatsApp
articles.nri_angle: An Indian founder who built his career entirely in India — no Valley pedigree — now runs a platform used by 3 billion people, while Meta's $900M CRED investment signals that India's fintech ecosystem has matured into a destination for strategic Big Tech capital.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oracle Quietly Cut 21,000 Jobs Last Year. It Blamed AI.
articles.excerpt: A regulatory filing reveals the scale of Oracle's AI-driven restructuring — and the 60-day visa clock it starts for thousands of Indian workers.
articles.image_caption: Oracle's former Redwood City headquarters in California
articles.nri_angle: Oracle is a major H-1B visa sponsor. For Indian professionals on work visas, these AI-driven layoffs trigger a 60-day grace period to find new sponsorship or leave the country — a personal crisis buried inside a corporate filing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Uber Blew Its AI Budget in Four Months. Now the Whole Industry Is Pulling Back.
articles.excerpt: The 'tokenmaxxing' era is over. Enterprises are discovering that AI tools cost more than the humans they were supposed to replace — and Indian IT could benefit from the reckoning.
articles.image_caption: A data centre server room — the physical infrastructure behind surging AI costs
articles.nri_angle: India's IT services industry — and the hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers at American tech companies — sits at the centre of this reckoning. The tokenmaxxing backlash creates both risk (more layoffs) and opportunity (AI governance consulting) for the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Launched Its Best AI Model the Same Week It Lost Two of Its Best Researchers. Then It Went to India.
articles.excerpt: Gemini 3 debuts with a massive reasoning upgrade and a pointed message: New Delhi will help write the rules for AI safety.
articles.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google, at a corporate event in 2023
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans work at and compete with the labs building these models; India-specific safety tools address digital fraud targeting NRI families back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foxconn's New Bengaluru Factory Just Shipped Its First iPhones. Apple Wants a Quarter of All Production in India.
articles.excerpt: The Devanahalli plant goes live as Apple targets 25% India manufacturing — but a massive Tata data breach reminds everyone what scale costs.
articles.image_caption: Smartphone circuit boards in production at an electronics manufacturing facility
articles.nri_angle: NRIs are invested in Tata and India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem; the iPhones they buy may soon be Made in India; high-skill roles in Apple's supply chain create reverse-migration opportunities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Persistent Systems Just Bet $1.1 Billion That Indian IT Can Buy Its Way Into Europe
articles.excerpt: The Pune-based firm's offer for Germany's Nagarro is among the largest cross-border deals in Indian tech history. Investors have questions.
articles.image_caption: Oleg Yunakov via wikimedia (BY-SA)
articles.nri_angle: The deal signals a new M&A-driven growth model for Indian IT, directly relevant to NRI investors and tech professionals watching the sector's AI-era transformation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Dropped the Rule That Was Keeping Starlink Out. The Satellite Race Is On.
articles.excerpt: New Delhi's decision to scrap a 20 per cent local sourcing mandate clears the path for Starlink, OneWeb and Amazon Kuiper to bring broadband to 1.4 billion people.
articles.image_caption: A SpaceX Starlink rocket launch carrying satellite broadband payloads into orbit
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with family in underserved rural India, satellite broadband could deliver reliable internet where fibre and 4G never reached — and Bharti-backed OneWeb makes it an investable thesis.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Banned Its Best AI Models. Japan and China Built Replacements in Two Weeks.
articles.excerpt: Sakana AI, Zhipu and 360 Security have launched Anthropic alternatives that sidestep US export controls. India, with no sovereign frontier model, is taking notes.
articles.image_caption: NVIDIA GPUs power the frontier AI models that the US has now restricted from export, spurring Asian competitors to build alternatives (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian developers and enterprises dependent on US AI models face overnight access risk; NRI engineers at American AI labs are caught between export controls and their own careers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NVIDIA Just Dethroned Jayshree Ullal's Arista in the Market She Built
articles.excerpt: The Indian-born CEO turned Arista into a networking giant. Now NVIDIA's platform play has seized the top spot in data centre Ethernet switching — and the implications run deeper than market share.
articles.image_caption: Arista Networks CEO Jayshree Ullal, the Indian-born engineer whose company just lost its top networking ranking to NVIDIA
articles.nri_angle: Indian-born Jayshree Ullal built Arista into a $100B networking giant; her company just lost the top spot to NVIDIA's platform approach — built partly by Indian engineers on H-1B visas at NVIDIA's Santa Clara and Bengaluru offices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Musk's Real AI Business: Renting Idle GPUs to Anthropic and Google for $2 Billion a Month
articles.excerpt: SpaceX's xAI data centres have locked in $76 billion in compute leases through 2029. The backstory involves a facility that couldn't train its own chatbot — and a global GPU famine that India can barely afford to watch from the sidelines.
articles.image_caption: Elon Musk, whose xAI subsidiary now earns over $2 billion monthly in GPU rental revenue (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's entire IndiaAI Mission GPU allocation is less than 5% of what Anthropic rents from one SpaceX facility. Indian engineers at Google, Anthropic, and NVIDIA are on both sides of these deals — building the models and designing the chips that drive compute demand.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Delhi Wants a Piece of India's AI Unicorn. It's Paying in GPUs.
articles.excerpt: The Indian government is acquiring a stake in Sarvam AI through subsidised compute — an unusual move that turns GPU access into equity and signals sovereign AI is now a matter of national strategy.
articles.image_caption: Ashwini Vaishnaw, India's Minister for Electronics and IT, whose ministry is converting GPU compute access into equity in AI startup Sarvam (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Sarvam is actively recruiting Indian-origin AI researchers from the US to build sovereign AI models for 22 Indian languages. The government equity stake signals India wants to build AI at home, not just export AI talent — a strategic shift that touches every NRI engineer in Silicon Valley.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Built Its Own Chip in Nine Months. Nvidia Should Pay Attention.
articles.excerpt: Jalapeño, a custom inference processor designed with Broadcom, marks OpenAI's first step toward owning the silicon that runs ChatGPT — and Indian chip designers are at the centre of what comes next.
articles.image_caption: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, whose company designed its first custom AI chip in nine months (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Broadcom's Indian design centres in Hyderabad and Bengaluru will iterate on Jalapeño's successors, and the custom-ASIC boom is creating high-value chip design jobs that align with India's semiconductor mission — directly relevant for NRI engineers and investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pichai's Worst Week: Google Lost a Nobel Laureate, a Transformer Co-Author, and $225 Billion
articles.excerpt: Two of AI's most important researchers left Google for its rivals in the same week. The stock recorded its largest-ever single-day market cap loss, and Gemini 3.5 Pro has been pushed to July.
articles.image_caption: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Alphabet and Google, at a 2023 event
articles.nri_angle: Sundar Pichai is the most prominent Indian-origin CEO in tech, and tens of thousands of Indian engineers at Google — many on H-1B visas — face career and equity implications from the talent exodus and stock decline.

articles.title: India's Payment Network Just Built Its Own AI. It Already Serves a Million Users.
articles.excerpt: NPCI's in-house language model FiMI is processing disputes in four languages, agentic payments are live in prototype, and the man who runs UPI says AI will bring the next 500 million users.
articles.image_caption: Bamboofirdaus via wikimedia (CC0)
articles.nri_angle: UPI's international expansion makes it a portable payment identity for NRIs abroad, and the AI layer — from FiMI to agentic commerce — represents the next wave of fintech value creation for diaspora investors watching India's digital infrastructure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Washington Is About to Unlock Anthropic's Fable 5. India's Quiet Diplomacy Helped.
articles.excerpt: After two weeks of backdoor negotiations at the Pax Silica Summit, the US is close to restoring access to the AI model it abruptly shut down — and India's IT Secretary forced the conversation.
articles.image_caption: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei — India is negotiating restored access to Claude after US export controls cut off foreign developers (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian developers and IT companies like TCS that were cut off from Claude Fable 5 on June 12 are about to regain access — but the episode has forced a reckoning over whether India can safely build its tech future on American AI platforms.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's VCs Just Poured $1.2 Billion into Deep Tech in Six Months. They're Not Funding Apps.
articles.excerpt: Drones, electric aircraft, gas turbines, and AI chips — India's venture capital scene is shifting from consumer apps to defence tech and hardware, and the money is moving fast.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons (CC)
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs in Silicon Valley, India's deep tech boom is creating the kind of technical challenge and equity upside that used to require staying in the Bay Area — defence drones, eVTOL aircraft, and sovereign AI chips are now fundable in Bengaluru.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
